boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Evanston-campus places for studying, making, art, landscape, and public programs, supported by current Northwestern sources.

cards.title: Norris University Center
cards.subtitle: 1999 Campus Drive, by the lakefront
cards.notes: Use this student center as a practical meeting point before an event, film, or campus errand; confirm the specific service or room you need on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A long-running campus hub for student activity and casual connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern describes Norris as its student-activity center since its 1973 dedication and says it offers artistic, leadership, movie, book, and social opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Located at 1999 Campus Drive; services and room availability vary.

cards.title: The Lakefill
cards.subtitle: Northwestern’s Lake Michigan lakefront
cards.notes: Take the lakefront paths for a reset between commitments, and use the open shoreline areas thoughtfully around walkers, beach users, and changing weather.
cards.short_summary: A campus lakefront landscape with paths, beaches, and skyline views.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern says its Evanston lakefront has trails and beaches and identifies warm-weather uses including picnics, jogging, walking, swimming, and sailing.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and beach access vary with weather and posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Information Commons
cards.subtitle: University Library, Level 1
cards.notes: Choose the open tables when you need to spread out with collaborators, then check the library’s room listings if your group needs a reservable space.
cards.short_summary: An open, group-oriented study area in University Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern Libraries lists the Information Commons on University Library Level 1 as open seating with group-study-space features.
cards.access_notes: Open seating; consult library hours and room information before visiting.

cards.title: Fourth Floor Towers
cards.subtitle: University Library, Level 4
cards.notes: Bring focused reading or writing here and treat it as a quiet setting; use another library area for conversation-heavy work or group meetings.
cards.short_summary: Quiet open seating high in University Library’s research towers.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern Libraries lists the Fourth Floor Towers at University Library Level 4 as open seating with a quiet feature.
cards.access_notes: Open seating; check current library building hours.

cards.title: Martin Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Deering Library, Level 3
cards.notes: Settle in with a book or laptop when quiet work is the goal, and use the connected University Library spaces if you need a different study setup.
cards.short_summary: A named quiet reading room in historic Deering Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern Libraries identifies the Martin Reading Room on Deering Library Level 3 as open seating with a quiet feature.
cards.access_notes: Open seating; verify Deering Library access and hours before going.

cards.title: Seeley G. Mudd Library
cards.subtitle: Mudd Hall, 2233 Tech Drive
cards.notes: Use its communal study areas for work near Tech, or reserve an eligible private room when your project needs a more contained setup.
cards.short_summary: A North Campus library with open and reservable study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern Libraries says Mudd Library offers open study spaces and reservable private spaces, and describes private and communal study options.
cards.access_notes: Open study is available; 24/7 unstaffed access is limited to Northwestern community members with an active Wildcard.

cards.title: The Garage
cards.subtitle: 2311 Campus Drive, Suite 2300
cards.notes: Visit during general-access hours to learn about the startup community; ask staff before planning fabrication, since equipment access is for registered users.
cards.short_summary: Northwestern’s startup hub with student ventures and prototyping tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern says The Garage houses student startups, classroom space, and fabrication equipment for student entrepreneurs.
cards.access_notes: General access is listed as 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; fabrication equipment requires registered-user access.

cards.title: Block Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 40 Arts Circle Drive
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit around the posted schedule, then consider a Block Cinema screening when offered; galleries and programs can change with exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art museum with galleries and a dedicated film venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Block Museum states that it is free and open to all, and describes three galleries plus free Block Cinema screenings.
cards.access_notes: The official visit page lists seasonal hours and notes a current summer closure before fall exhibitions open September 9.

cards.title: Shakespeare Garden
cards.subtitle: East of Sheridan Road, near Garrett Place
cards.notes: Walk through the enclosed garden slowly to notice the planting beds, sundial, and memorial; keep to paths and respect the planted areas.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed historic garden designed by Jens Jensen.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern’s campus map says the garden was designed by Jens Jensen and includes flower beds, a sundial, a garden seat, and Shakespeare-related plantings.
cards.source_title: Northwestern University Campus Maps: Shakespeare Garden
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden; access and conditions depend on campus operations and weather.

cards.title: Dearborn Observatory
cards.subtitle: 2131 Tech Drive
cards.notes: For an evening visit, use the official schedule and arrive for the walk-in window if available; dress for the weather because the dome is not climate controlled.
cards.short_summary: A historic observatory offering public Friday-night viewing.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern Physics and Astronomy states that Dearborn’s Friday-night tours are free and open to the public, with a walk-in hour.
cards.access_notes: Free Friday tours: April–September walk-in 10–11 p.m.; October–March walk-in 9–10 p.m. The dome requires multiple staircases.
